newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS AGREE ON THREE-YEAR DEAL WITH TOP PICK.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS AGREE ON THREE-YEAR DEAL WITH TOP PICK.

text.p: Centre Joe Thornton, the first overall pick in the June NHL draft, agreed to terms on a three-year contract with the Boston Bruins, the team said Monday.
"Quite obviously, we're thrilled that this process has ended with this agreement," said Bruins assistant general manager Mike O'Connell, who did not reveal terms of the deal.
"We've made it clear since before the draft how excited we were about Joe's future with the Bruins. He's big, strong and has all the skills you look for in a player, with the attitude to match."
Thornton, who turned 18 July 2, was the first 17-year-old selected first overall since the Buffalo Sabres tabbed Pierre Turgeon in 1987.
Thornton will join a Bruins team which failed to make the playoffs for the first time in 30 years.
After a 26-47-9 campaign, the Bruins fired coach Steve Kasper in April and named Pat Burns as his successor in May.

Nicknamed "Big Bird," the 6-4 (1.93 m), 198-pound (90-kg) Thornton finished second in the Ontario Junior Hockey League scoring race with 41 goals and 81 assists for 122 points in 59 games with Sault Ste. Marie.
OHL coaches named Thornton as the best faceoff man in his division and he was the youngest member of Canada's gold-medal team at the 1997 World Junior Championships.
